sources_considered.why: Mozilla's summary of its review of 47 LLMs' training data.
The report landing page. It is useful background but does not give the 64% figure in the text that could be read.
Bears on whether expressed political views come from pretraining or post-training.
Says the same as the arXiv abstract on this point.

receipt.public_excerpt: the study analyzed 47 LLMs published between 2019 and October 2023 that power text generators and found at least 64% of them were trained on Common Crawl.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that many LLMs share a major data source, which partly supports the overlap claim. But 64% is short of 'pretty much every', the review stops at 2023, and it does not test any effect on views.

receipt.public_excerpt: our results provide preliminary evidence for the intriguing hypothesis that the embedding of political preferences into LLMs might be happening mostly post-pretraining.

evidence_items.explanation: Preliminary evidence that the shared political lean comes mainly from fine-tuning, not shared pretraining data. This cuts against Marcus's explanation, but the author says it is not conclusive.

unresolved_gaps: The training data of major 2024–2025 models (GPT-4o, Claude 3.x, Gemini 2.x, Grok 3) is largely undisclosed, so the overlap cannot be measured.
No controlled study isolates shared pretraining data as the cause of models' views clustering.
